project.name: financial-sentiment-analyzer
project.description: An end-to-end ML pipeline for classifying financial text sentiment, with classical TF-IDF baselines and FinBERT models, out-of-domain evaluation on real financial news with bootstrap confidence intervals, SHAP explainability, an LLM benchmark and RAG Q&A, a FastAPI inference service, and a Streamlit dashboard.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Streamlit entrypoint and router that sets page config, registers all 14 pages into grouped st.navigation sections (Overview, Analyze, Explain, Evaluate, Labs), and renders the shared CSS and sidebar once so model selection persists across page switches.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses st.navigation/st.Page (Streamlit's newer multipage API) instead of the legacy pages/ directory, so the sidebar is rendered once per run in the router rather than on every page.

nodes.name: home.py
nodes.summary: Dashboard front page that presents headline results (SVM in-domain test/CV macro-F1, out-of-domain collapse, FinBERT fine-tuned score) with bootstrap confidence intervals, reading numbers from results/*.json with hard-coded conservative fallbacks so the page never drifts from evaluation artifacts.

nodes.name: shared.py
nodes.summary: Thin compatibility/barrel layer that re-exports the design-system tokens and components from ui.py under one import surface for all pages, preserving historical names like inject_css and create_probability_chart.
nodes.languageNotes: Explicit __all__ with re-exports; adds src/ to sys.path for backwards compatibility since pages run as scripts, not as a package.

nodes.name: ui.py
nodes.summary: Centralised FinSight design system: color/sentiment tokens, global CSS, a registered Plotly template, reusable HTML components (page headers, KPI strips, verdict cards, probability bands, term tables, interval charts) and the model loader/sidebar that switches between in-process SentimentPredictor and a remote FastAPI client via FINSIGHT_API_URL.
nodes.languageNotes: Accessibility is a design rule: every sentiment label pairs color with a glyph and word, and text colors meet WCAG AA. st.cache_resource caches loaded models across reruns; contextmanager-based exhibit/chart_container wrap figures with numbered captions.

nodes.name: 10_Ask_the_News.py
nodes.summary: Retrieval-augmented Q&A page over the 2,388 real financial headlines: resolves LLM provider (Anthropic/OpenRouter/OpenAI) and API keys from env or Streamlit secrets, builds a cached embedding index via rag_news, answers questions with cited headlines and per-headline sentiment from the active model.
nodes.languageNotes: Gracefully degrades: stops with a status banner if LangChain is missing or keys are absent; only API-based embeddings are cached to disk since local ones rebuild in seconds.

nodes.name: 1_Single_Analysis.py
nodes.summary: Flagship single-text analysis page: classifies one sentence with the active model, shows a verdict card with class probabilities, the TF-IDF terms that drove the decision, and an optional LLM-written explanation.

nodes.name: 2_Batch_Processing.py
nodes.summary: Batch processing page implementing an upload, validate, preview, analyze, summarize, export flow for CSV/text inputs, with aggregate sentiment KPIs, distribution charts, an LLM market-outlook summary and downloadable results.

nodes.name: 3_Explainability.py
nodes.summary: Explainability page combining local explanations (per-term TF-IDF weight times coefficient, highlighted inline in the sentence) with global SHAP feature importance across the dataset when the optional shap module is available.
nodes.languageNotes: Optional dependency pattern: SHAP import wrapped in try/except with a SHAP_AVAILABLE flag.

nodes.name: 4_Word_Insights.py
nodes.summary: Word Insights page visualising the vocabulary each TF-IDF baseline model weights most heavily per sentiment class, as bar charts and term tables.

nodes.name: 5_Deep_Analysis.py
nodes.summary: Deep Analysis page running advanced rule-based NLP (Loughran-McDonald lexicon, entity extraction, linguistic measurements) and a deterministic chain-of-thought reasoning trace alongside the model verdict.
nodes.languageNotes: Advanced NLP modules are optional; the page checks ADVANCED_NLP_AVAILABLE and degrades gracefully.

nodes.name: 6_Model_Info.py
nodes.summary: Model registry page showing the selected model's PhraseBank test metrics (n=226), 5-fold cross-validation results, interval charts comparing models and a per-class breakdown, all read from saved result artifacts.

nodes.name: 7_Sentiment_Trends.py
nodes.summary: Generalization page reporting cross-dataset (out-of-domain) metrics with bootstrap intervals, plus a synthetic sentiment-versus-stock-price time-series demo and correlation analysis via scipy.
nodes.languageNotes: Makes the domain-shift story explicit: high in-domain scores versus collapsed out-of-domain macro-F1, with the time-series section clearly labelled as a synthetic demo.

nodes.name: 8_Error_Analysis.py
nodes.summary: Error analysis page that re-runs a baseline model on a data split, builds a per-sentence correctness/confidence table, and surfaces confusion patterns, confident mistakes and model weaknesses.

nodes.name: 9_Stock_Prediction_Extension.py
nodes.summary: Experimental Labs page that drives the nested stock-prediction workflow (price download, live news fetch, FinBERT scoring, feature engineering, LSTM training, next-day direction prediction) and charts price/sentiment timelines with the headlines used.

nodes.name: benchmark_finbert.py
nodes.summary: Script that benchmarks the off-the-shelf ProsusAI FinBERT model on the same held-out PhraseBank test split as the baselines and appends accuracy/F1/precision/recall to results/evaluation_results.json, so the README comparison table covers every claimed model on equal footing.

nodes.name: run_finbert_benchmark
nodes.summary: Runs pre-trained FinBERT over the test set and computes accuracy, macro/weighted F1, precision and recall.

nodes.name: save_to_evaluation_results

nodes.name: evaluate.py
nodes.summary: Central evaluation module: scores baseline joblib pipelines and fine-tuned transformers on a split, computes accuracy/macro-F1/precision/recall, plots confusion matrices, builds a model comparison table, runs error analysis on misclassifications, and persists results to JSON.

nodes.name: compute_metrics

nodes.name: print_evaluation_report

nodes.name: plot_confusion_matrix

nodes.name: compare_models

nodes.name: error_analysis

nodes.name: explain.py

nodes.languageNotes: Optional import guarded by try/except ImportError keeps the module usable when the lexicons module is missing.

nodes.name: get_feature_importance_summary

nodes.name: finbert_pretrained.py

nodes.languageNotes: Pins a model revision constant for reproducible, supply-chain-safe Hub downloads; get_finbert caches a module-level instance.

nodes.name: PretrainedFinBERT

nodes.name: integrate_news.py
nodes.summary: Cross-dataset integration: scores news headlines with a trained model, aggregates them into daily per-ticker sentiment, correlates sentiment with stock returns, feeds the Streamlit trends page, and measures true out-of-distribution generalization on the real, human-labeled zeroshot/twitter-financial-news-sentiment set. Explicitly flags the bundled sample_news.csv as synthetic so correlation results are not over-claimed.
nodes.languageNotes: Distinguishes synthetic demo data from a real licensed OOD dataset in module constants - a deliberate honesty guard against inflated generalization claims.

nodes.name: compute_sentiment_stock_correlation

Supports FinBERT, DistilBERT, RoBERTa, BERT and DeBERTa backbones.
nodes.languageNotes: Custom training loop instead of the HF Trainer gives explicit control over class weights, warmup and device placement.

nodes.name: train_transformer

nodes.summary: PyTorch Dataset that tokenizes texts with padding/truncation and returns input tensors with labels.

nodes.summary: Wrapper over a Hugging Face sequence-classification model providing training loop (AdamW, warmup, class weights), evaluation, prediction and save/load.

nodes.summary: Unified inference facade (SentimentPredictor) over baseline joblib pipelines, the voting ensemble, pre-trained FinBERT and fine-tuned transformers, with confidence/probability outputs, file batch prediction, and a model discovery function. nodes.name: llm_provider.py
nodes.summary: Single place that resolves which LLM provider (Anthropic Claude, OpenRouter or OpenAI), model and temperature to use from arguments and FINSIGHT_* environment variables, and builds the matching LangChain chat model. Isolates vendor differences (OpenRouter reuses ChatOpenAI with a custom base URL and uses function-calling for structured output) so the benchmark and RAG code stay provider-agnostic.
nodes.languageNotes: Provider SDKs (langchain_anthropic, langchain_openai) are imported lazily inside make_chat_model so only the selected provider's package must be installed.

nodes.name: get_provider
nodes.summary: Resolves the provider name: explicit argument, then FINSIGHT_LLM_PROVIDER, then whichever API key is present (anthropic, openrouter, openai order), defaulting to anthropic; rejects unknown names.

nodes.name: get_model_name
nodes.summary: Picks the model id from the argument, FINSIGHT_LLM_MODEL, or the provider default (Claude Haiku for Anthropic); raises a clear error for OpenRouter/OpenAI, which deliberately have no default.

nodes.name: get_temperature
nodes.summary: Reads FINSIGHT_LLM_TEMPERATURE, defaulting to 0 for repeatable answers and returning None ('none') for models that reject the parameter.

nodes.name: has_api_key
nodes.summary: Reports whether the API key environment variable for the resolved provider is set, letting callers skip LLM features gracefully.

nodes.name: make_chat_model
nodes.summary: Factory returning a LangChain ChatAnthropic or ChatOpenAI instance with timeout, retries, token cap and temperature; for OpenRouter it points ChatOpenAI at OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible URL with its key and app header.

nodes.name: with_structured_output
nodes.summary: Binds a Pydantic schema to a chat model's output, using function_calling on OpenRouter because tool calling is more widely supported across its routed vendors than JSON-schema mode.

nodes.name: llm_sentiment.py
nodes.summary: LLM sentiment classifier used to benchmark zero-shot and few-shot Claude/OpenRouter/OpenAI prompting against fine-tuned FinBERT on real financial headlines, measuring accuracy, cost and latency. Key design choices: Pydantic Literal structured output (invalid answers scored wrong), temperature 0, few-shot examples drawn only from the PhraseBank training split to avoid leakage, a disk cache keyed by model/prompt version/mode/text, and threaded concurrent calls.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses typing.Literal inside a Pydantic model to constrain LLM output to three labels, and ThreadPoolExecutor.map to parallelise I/O-bound API calls while preserving input order.

nodes.name: SentimentLabel
nodes.summary: Pydantic schema whose Literal field restricts the model's answer to negative, neutral or positive.

nodes.name: few_shot_examples
nodes.summary: Samples a balanced, seeded set of examples per class from the PhraseBank training CSV and interleaves classes so example order does not hint at the answer.

nodes.name: build_messages
nodes.summary: Builds the chat message list for one headline: investor-perspective system prompt, optional few-shot examples as prior human/ai turns, then the headline.

nodes.name: make_runnable
nodes.summary: Creates a provider-resolved chat model capped at 64 output tokens and wraps it with SentimentLabel structured output, keeping the raw response for token usage.

nodes.name: AnswerCache
nodes.summary: Append-only JSON-lines cache of LLM answers loaded into memory at startup so reruns of the benchmark never pay for the same call twice.

nodes.name: _call_one
nodes.summary: Runs one LLM call and returns label (or None), input/output tokens, latency and error; exceptions are recorded instead of raised so a long benchmark keeps going.

nodes.name: classify
nodes.summary: Classifies a list of texts in order, reusing valid cached answers and dispatching the rest concurrently via a thread pool, caching only valid labels.

nodes.name: summarize_usage
nodes.summary: Aggregates a run's tokens, optional USD cost from caller-supplied per-1M-token prices (None rather than a guess), p50/p95 latency, invalid answers, errors and cache hits.

nodes.name: rag_news.py
nodes.summary: Retrieval-augmented Q&A over 2,388 real financial headlines: embeds headlines into a LangChain InMemoryVectorStore (local TF-IDF+LSA embeddings by default, OpenAI optional, index cached on disk), retrieves top-k by cosine similarity, and asks a chat model for a structured answer with citations. Trade-offs: local embeddings avoid a second API key (Anthropic has no embeddings API); citations outside the retrieved set are dropped and the prompt treats headlines as untrusted data to resist prompt injection.
nodes.languageNotes: LocalLSAEmbeddings duck-types LangChain's Embeddings interface (sync and async methods) instead of subclassing it, so it plugs into the vector store without a hosted model.

nodes.name: NewsAnswer
nodes.summary: Pydantic schema the chat model must return: an answer string plus the list of headline numbers it cites.

nodes.name: get_embedding_kind
nodes.summary: Resolves the embedding backend ('local' or 'openai') from the argument or FINSIGHT_EMBEDDINGS, validating the value.

nodes.name: get_embedding_model
nodes.summary: Returns the embedding model name: the fixed local LSA name, or the OpenAI model from argument/env/default text-embedding-3-small.

nodes.name: LocalLSAEmbeddings
nodes.summary: Latent semantic analysis embeddings: word 1-2 gram TF-IDF (keeping cashtags like $TSLA, dropping question filler words) reduced with truncated SVD and L2-normalised, fitted on the corpus so no download or API is needed.

nodes.name: load_corpus
nodes.summary: Loads the real financial news CSV and assigns a stable integer id per row.

nodes.name: build_index
nodes.summary: Builds or loads an InMemoryVectorStore over the headlines, keyed on disk by embedding model and a hash of the corpus so the corpus is embedded only once.

nodes.name: retrieve
nodes.summary: Runs similarity search and returns the top-k headlines numbered 1..k with ids, gold labels and similarity scores for citation.

nodes.name: build_messages
nodes.summary: Formats the grounded-answer prompt: system rules plus the numbered headlines and the user's question.

nodes.name: make_answer_runnable
nodes.summary: Creates a provider-resolved chat model (600-token cap, 2 retries) bound to the NewsAnswer structured output.

nodes.name: make_embeddings
nodes.summary: Factory returning local LSA embeddings fitted on the corpus or LangChain OpenAIEmbeddings, depending on the configured kind.

nodes.name: answer_question
nodes.summary: Produces a grounded answer, validating citations: deduplicates them, keeps only numbers present in the retrieved sources and reports invented ones as dropped_citations.

nodes.name: sentiment_mix
nodes.summary: Computes the share of negative, neutral and positive labels among retrieved headlines so users can sanity-check the answer.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Docker build-context exclusion list that keeps virtualenvs, git history, caches, notebooks, tests, docs and the nested project's scratch/venv folders out of the image, shrinking the context and preventing local artifacts leaking into containers.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage python:3.10-slim image for the Streamlit dashboard (UI tier): installs CPU-only PyTorch first to avoid the multi-GB CUDA wheel, then requirements-deploy.txt, copies src/, app/, models/, data/ and the nested stock-prediction extension, exposes 8501 with a stdlib-based healthcheck and runs app/app.py headless.
nodes.languageNotes: Layer ordering installs dependencies before copying code so code edits reuse cached pip layers; the HEALTHCHECK uses python urllib because slim images ship without curl. Baking models/ and data/ into the image trades image size for zero-download startup.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Compose stack for the split architecture: Streamlit UI -> nginx load balancer -> horizontally scalable FastAPI replicas (--scale api=N), with a shared Redis instance backing rate limiting across replicas; optional API key passed through from the host env.
nodes.languageNotes: Only the lb and ui publish host ports; api and redis use expose so they are reachable solely on the internal network, and the API trusts proxy headers (FINSIGHT_TRUST_PROXY) since requests arrive via nginx.

nodes.name: redis
nodes.summary: Redis 7 (alpine) instance on the internal network providing a shared store so rate-limit counters stay consistent across all API replicas.

nodes.name: api
nodes.summary: FastAPI inference service built from Dockerfile.api; stateless and scalable via --scale, configured with optional API key, the Redis URL and proxy trust for real client IPs.

nodes.name: lb
nodes.summary: nginx load balancer mounting deploy/nginx.conf read-only and publishing port 8080, distributing requests across the api replicas.

nodes.name: ui
nodes.summary: Streamlit dashboard built from the main Dockerfile on port 8501; points FINSIGHT_API_URL at the load balancer so predictions run on the API tier rather than in-process.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions CI workflow that runs on push/PR to main/master: installs the lightweight requirements-ci.txt on Python 3.10, then runs Ruff lint and format checks over src/app/api/tests, mypy on utils.py and preprocess.py, and the pytest suite. Using a slim CI requirements file and scoped mypy keeps the pipeline fast and avoids pulling heavy ML dependencies like torch.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a single-entry Python version matrix, making it easy to extend to more versions later; mypy is run incrementally on only the most stable modules rather than the whole codebase.

nodes.name: retrain.yml
nodes.summary: Scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (monthly cron at 05:00 UTC on the 1st, plus manual workflow_dispatch) that runs scripts/retrain.py to retrain baselines, cross-validate, evaluate and update the model registry, re-runs the test suite, and uploads results/, models/registry.json and joblib models as a 14-day artifact. Artifacts are uploaded for human review rather than auto-committed, a deliberate safeguard against silently shipping regressed models.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines a cron schedule with workflow_dispatch so retraining can also be triggered on demand; upload-artifact with retention-days bounds storage cost.

nodes.name: Dockerfile.api
nodes.summary: Container image for the FastAPI inference service only: installs CPU-only PyTorch first to keep the image small, then requirements-deploy.txt plus a Redis client, copies just src/, api/ and models/, and runs uvicorn with 2 workers behind a /health HEALTHCHECK. Designed as the horizontally scaled API tier in the split UI + API + nginx architecture.
nodes.languageNotes: Installing torch from the PyTorch CPU wheel index before the requirements file prevents pip from pulling the ~2 GB CUDA build; layer ordering (requirements before source COPY) maximizes Docker cache reuse.

nodes.summary: Lightweight model registry CLI that snapshots every trained artifact (TF-IDF baselines, fine-tuned transformers, stock LSTMs) with SHA-256 hash, size, timestamp and latest metrics into models/registry.json, with optional best-effort MLflow logging.

nodes.name: shap_explain.py
nodes.summary: SHAP explainability module for the TF-IDF baselines that computes exact SHAP values (linear SHAP for linear models, per-tree TreeSHAP summed over boosting stages with an additivity check for multi-class gradient boosting, TreeExplainer for random forests, KernelSHAP fallback) and produces top-feature JSON reports and summary plots.
nodes.languageNotes: Works around shap.TreeExplainer's lack of multi-class GradientBoostingClassifier support by exploiting that each class score is a learning-rate-scaled sum of regression trees.

nodes.name: train.py
nodes.summary: Training entry point for financial sentiment models: builds TF-IDF + classifier pipelines, trains baselines and a soft-voting ensemble, delegates transformer fine-tuning to model.py, runs stratified k-fold cross-validation, and GridSearchCV tuning that writes tuned_*.joblib unless --promote-tuned is given.

nodes.name: _hash_file
nodes.summary: Computes a truncated (12-char) SHA-256 digest of a model artifact by streaming it in 8 KB chunks.

nodes.name: _load_eval_metrics
nodes.summary: Loads results/evaluation_results.json and maps each model name to its accuracy, macro-F1 and weighted-F1, tolerating missing or malformed files.

nodes.name: _finetune_metrics
nodes.summary: Reads metrics for a *_finetuned transformer from results/finetune_results_<model>.json, returning accuracy, F1, dataset and split sizes when present.

nodes.name: _discover_artifacts
nodes.summary: Globs the models directory for baseline_*.joblib files and *_finetuned/model.safetensors weights, plus stock-prediction LSTM checkpoints when that external dataset exists.

nodes.name: build_registry
nodes.summary: Builds the registry snapshot dict: one entry per discovered artifact with hash, size, mtime, joined metrics, and a flag marking un-fetched Git LFS pointer files.

nodes.name: update_registry
nodes.summary: Builds the registry and writes it as JSON to models/registry.json, returning the snapshot.

nodes.name: log_to_mlflow
nodes.summary: Best-effort MLflow logging that creates a run per registered model with artifact/hash tags, size param and numeric metrics; returns False if MLflow is not installed.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Argparse CLI entry handling --update, --mlflow and --show to refresh, log or print the model registry.

nodes.name: _linear_shap
nodes.summary: Computes exact linear SHAP values per class as coef times the deviation of each feature from its training-set mean.

nodes.name: _gradient_boosting_shap
nodes.summary: Computes exact SHAP for multi-class GradientBoostingClassifier by running TreeExplainer on every boosted regression tree, scaling by learning rate, summing per class, and verifying additivity against decision_function.

nodes.name: compute_shap_values
nodes.summary: Dispatches to the appropriate SHAP method for a classifier (linear, boosted trees, TreeExplainer, or KernelSHAP fallback) and returns per-class values with the method name.

nodes.name: get_shap_explanation
nodes.summary: Loads a saved baseline pipeline and a sample of a data split, computes SHAP values against a training-mean background, and returns per-class top contributing TF-IDF features with their mean attributions.

nodes.name: save_shap_results
nodes.summary: Runs get_shap_explanation for a model/split and writes the result to a JSON file in the results directory.

nodes.name: generate_shap_plot
nodes.summary: Produces a SHAP summary plot of TF-IDF feature contributions for a baseline model on a sampled split, saving it as an image or displaying it.

nodes.name: create_baseline_pipeline
nodes.summary: Factory that builds a scikit-learn Pipeline of TF-IDF vectorizer plus one of six classifiers (logreg, svm, naive_bayes, random_forest, gradient_boosting, mlp).

nodes.name: train_baseline
nodes.summary: Trains one baseline pipeline on the train split, evaluates accuracy and F1 on validation, and optionally saves it as baseline_<name>.joblib.

nodes.name: train_all_baselines
nodes.summary: Trains every baseline classifier in turn and logs the best by validation macro-F1.

nodes.name: train_ensemble
nodes.summary: Trains a soft-voting ensemble of calibrated LinearSVC, logistic regression and random forest on shared TF-IDF features, evaluates it, and saves it.

nodes.name: load_model
nodes.summary: Loads a saved joblib model from the models directory, raising FileNotFoundError if absent.

nodes.name: train_transformer
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper that lazily imports model.train_transformer and fine-tunes a transformer (FinBERT, DistilBERT, RoBERTa, BERT).

nodes.name: train_all_models
nodes.summary: Orchestrates training of all baselines and optionally transformers, collecting results and reporting the best model.

nodes.name: cross_validate_baselines
nodes.summary: Runs stratified k-fold cross-validation of all baseline pipelines on combined train+val data, reporting mean/std accuracy and F1 and saving results JSON.

nodes.name: tune_hyperparameters
nodes.summary: Grid-searches TF-IDF and classifier hyperparameters for SVM and gradient boosting with stratified CV, saving the best estimators as tuned_*.joblib (or overwriting baselines when promote=True) and writing tuning results JSON.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README, which covers the whole system: TF-IDF and FinBERT models, real-news out-of-domain (OOD) evaluation with bootstrap CIs, the LangChain LLM benchmark and RAG Q&A, the FastAPI service, the Streamlit dashboard and four deployment options. The interview guide adds the headline result to remember: macro-F1 is 0.90 in-domain, falls to 0.46 on real news and recovers to 0.84 after news fine-tuning. Interviewers usually open with 'pitch this project in two minutes' and 'what problem does it solve, and for whom?'.

tour.title: Problem and Datasets
tour.description: The data manifest lists every dataset: Financial PhraseBank AllAgree (2,264 sentences, stratified 80/10/10 split, seed 42) for training, synthetic headlines marked as demo-only, and the MIT-licensed Twitter Financial News set (~2,388 headlines) that serves as the real OOD benchmark. The fetch script downloads that set from Hugging Face and maps Bearish/Bullish/Neutral onto the project's labels. Expect questions such as 'why use the AllAgree subset?', 'how did you handle class imbalance?' and 'why test on a second dataset?'.

tour.title: Preprocessing and Shared Foundations
tour.description: preprocess.py loads PhraseBank at a chosen annotator-agreement level, cleans the text, encodes labels as integers and writes stratified train/val/test CSVs. Training, evaluation and SHAP all read those files. utils.py is the module most other files depend on (highest fan-in): it holds the label mappings, path helpers and logging setup. Interviewers often ask how you prevent data leakage between splits, why the splits are stratified, and why the label encoding lives in one shared module.

tour.title: Baselines, CV and Tuning
tour.description: train.py builds TF-IDF pipelines for six classical classifiers (logistic regression, Naive Bayes, calibrated SVM, random forest, gradient boosting, MLP) plus a soft-voting ensemble. It adds stratified k-fold cross-validation and GridSearchCV tuning, all fed by the splits from Step 3. Likely questions: 'why build a strong classical baseline before using transformers?', 'why calibrate the SVM?' and 'why report CV scores as well as a single test score on 226 sentences?'.
tour.languageLesson: scikit-learn Pipelines bundle the TF-IDF vectorizer and the classifier into one object. During cross-validation the vectorizer is then fit only on each training fold, which prevents leakage, and the whole pipeline can be saved and loaded as a single joblib artifact.

tour.title: FinBERT Fine-Tuning
tour.description: model.py wraps AutoModelForSequenceClassification with AdamW, linear warmup and optional class-weighted cross-entropy to optimise macro-F1 on imbalanced labels, and it supports FinBERT, DistilBERT, RoBERTa, BERT and DeBERTa backbones. finbert_pretrained.py runs the off-the-shelf ProsusAI/finbert model and remaps its native label order to the project's scheme. finetune_finbert_news.py fine-tunes on in-domain news to test whether the OOD gap comes from domain mismatch. Interviewers ask about label-order bugs, class weighting, the zero-shot vs fine-tuned trade-off, and GPU/AMP choices.
tour.languageLesson: Hugging Face models store id2label/label2id in config.json. If a checkpoint's label order differs from yours, you must remap the outputs explicitly. The guard test here checks the committed config against the project's LABEL_MAP.

tour.title: Unified Prediction Interface
tour.description: SentimentPredictor in predict.py is a single interface over the joblib baselines, the voting ensemble, pre-trained FinBERT and the fine-tuned transformers. It returns labels, confidences and probabilities, and it falls back to Hugging Face Hub repos when local weights are missing or are only Git LFS pointers. Both the dashboard and the API call this one class, so it is the hinge of the architecture. Expect 'how do you serve heterogeneous models behind one interface?' and 'how do large weights reach a cloud deployment?'.

tour.title: Evaluation and Bootstrap CIs
tour.description: evaluate.py scores every model on a split (accuracy, macro-F1, precision/recall, confusion matrices, error analysis). stats.py is the one shared implementation of macro-F1 and percentile-bootstrap CIs, so baselines, FinBERT and the LLM are compared the same way. bootstrap_ci.py runs 2,000 resamples on the small test split and on real news, rebuilding (true, predicted) pairs from saved confusion matrices. Interviewers probe 'why macro-F1 rather than accuracy?', 'what does a CI tell you on n=226?' and 'how does a percentile bootstrap work?'.

tour.title: Out-of-Domain Generalization
tour.description: This step holds the project's central finding. compare_ood.py combines the per-model results on real news into one comparison file. The Generalization dashboard page reports those cross-dataset metrics with bootstrap intervals, and the model card records the in-domain vs OOD gap and its limitations. The integration test runs the SVM on the real news set and skips cleanly when the artifacts are missing. Be ready to explain why macro-F1 collapses from about 0.90 to 0.46 on headlines, how in-domain fine-tuning recovers it to about 0.84, and what that says about domain shift.

tour.title: Explainability with SHAP
tour.description: shap_explain.py uses TreeExplainer for tree ensembles and LinearExplainer for linear models on TF-IDF features, and extracts the top contributing features per class. The lighter explain.py ranks words by TF-IDF weight times coefficient and uses the Loughran-McDonald lexicon to give each word a direction. The Explainability page shows both local and global explanations. Interviewers ask why the explainer choice depends on model type, how faithful coefficient-based explanations are, and why that matters for finance users.

tour.title: LLM Benchmark and RAG
tour.description: llm_provider.py builds a LangChain chat model for Claude, OpenRouter or OpenAI based on environment variables, so the code above it does not depend on any one vendor. llm_sentiment.py and llm_benchmark.py compare zero-shot and few-shot prompting against fine-tuned FinBERT on the same 2,388 headlines with the bootstrap macro-F1 from Step 7. They use Pydantic structured output (invalid answers count as wrong), temperature 0, leakage-free few-shot examples and a disk cache, and they also report cost and latency. rag_news.py answers questions over the headlines using local TF-IDF+LSA embeddings, with citations and a guard against prompt injection. Expect 'LLM or fine-tuned model: when and why?', 'how did you control cost?' and 'how do you stop hallucinated citations?'.
tour.languageLesson: LangChain's with_structured_output binds a Pydantic schema to the model. Using a Literal['negative','neutral','positive'] field means any answer outside those labels fails validation, so free-text answers cannot slip through.

tour.title: Serving: FastAPI and Monitoring
tour.description: api/main.py wraps the same SentimentPredictor from Step 6 behind /health, /models, /predict, /predict/batch and /metrics. It adds Pydantic validation, optional API-key auth and slowapi rate limiting (backed by Redis when configured), and it caches predictors per worker. monitoring.py provides a stdlib-only structured logger, a JSON-lines audit trail and a thread-safe metrics registry with latency percentiles. registry.py hashes every artifact and records its metrics in a versioned registry.json. Interviewers ask how rate limits stay consistent across replicas, what you monitor in production, and how you trace a prediction back to a model version.
tour.languageLesson: In FastAPI, Pydantic request models validate input before the handler runs. Blank, oversized or empty-batch payloads are rejected automatically with a 422 response, which keeps the inference code free of validation checks.

tour.title: Streamlit Dashboard
tour.description: app.py is the Streamlit router: it registers 14 pages into Overview, Analyze, Explain, Evaluate and Labs sections and renders the sidebar once so the selected model persists across pages. ui.py is the design system and model loader. It switches between the in-process SentimentPredictor and api_client.py's RemotePredictor, depending on whether FINSIGHT_API_URL is set, which lets the UI and the model service scale independently. Likely questions: 'why separate the UI from inference?' and 'how do you keep the UI honest about model limitations?'.

tour.title: Test Suite
tour.description: The pytest suite runs offline: test_api.py uses FastAPI's TestClient to check validation, metrics and API-key enforcement. The LLM and RAG tests use stub runnables and DeterministicFakeEmbedding, so they need no API keys and cost nothing. test_page_imports.py parses each dashboard page and checks that every imported symbol actually exists in the project modules. Interviewers ask how you test non-deterministic, paid LLM code and what tests guard the serving path.

tour.title: CI/CD and Retraining
tour.description: ci.yml runs on every push or PR: it installs the slim requirements-ci.txt, runs Ruff lint and format checks, mypy on core modules, and the tests from Step 13, without pulling in torch. retrain.yml runs monthly through retrain.py (train, 5-fold CV, evaluate, refresh registry) and uploads the artifacts for human review instead of auto-committing them, which guards against silently shipping a regressed model. Expect 'how do you keep CI fast with heavy ML dependencies?' and 'why not auto-deploy retrained models?'.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows combine 'on' triggers such as push, pull_request, schedule (cron) and workflow_dispatch. Jobs run steps in order, and actions/upload-artifact keeps outputs for a set retention period (14 days here).

tour.title: Containerized Deployment
tour.description: docker-compose.yml wires the split architecture: the Streamlit UI calls an nginx load balancer, which spreads requests across horizontally scaled FastAPI replicas (--scale api=N). A shared Redis instance keeps rate-limit counters consistent across replicas. Dockerfile.api installs CPU-only PyTorch first to keep the image small, copies only src/, api/ and models/, and runs uvicorn behind a /health check. nginx.conf re-resolves the replicas through Docker DNS on each request and forwards client IPs for the rate limiter. Interviewers ask how you would scale this, why each tier is stateless, and what changes in a cloud deployment.
tour.languageLesson: In docker-compose, services on the same network reach each other by service name. Using a variable proxy_pass in nginx makes it re-resolve that name through Docker's embedded DNS, so replicas added with --scale join the load-balancing rotation.
